headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because TREK handles secrets and collaborative outputs while Great Expectations can ingest and write files, but direct prompt-injection evidence is limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations exposes file I/O for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while TREK has MCP and collaborative real-time inputs. The pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser that would make injection default, so the main pathway is manual or indirect content transfer rather than a strong default hijack.
conditions: IF TREK content is copied into Great Expectations documentation or test files as trusted instructions
IF an MCP bridge is configured to pass TREK text directly into Great Expectations prompts or parsers
mitigations: Disable any MCP bridge between the tools
Require manual review of copied text before use
Separate TREK exports from Great Expectations working files
Use a read-only handoff folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and logs, and it writes to ./data/travel.db and ./uploads/. Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation and can read data sources. If they share a workspace, sensitive TREK data can be exposed through Great Expectations outputs or validation artifacts; the pairwise leakage risk is substantial.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same filesystem or mounted workspace
IF TREK secrets or reservation data are placed in files that Great Expectations reads or validates
mitigations: Keep separate directories and mounts
Exclude secrets and logs from Great Expectations scans
Redact sensitive fields before validation
Restrict TREK uploads and logs to a private path
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files; TREK has allowlisted network egress, browser use, MCP, and collaborative multi-instance sessions. Their write surfaces overlap only indirectly, so conflict is plausible in shared resources but not clearly destructive by default. Uncertainty remains because no locking or shared-state protocol is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF TREK and Great Expectations are run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run one agent at a time for shared files
Use file locks on shared artifacts
Avoid package installs during concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in and multiple downstream APIs, while Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation. If TREK consumes Great Expectations outputs as authoritative without verification, bad validation or documentation can cascade into incorrect travel actions. The pair does not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Great Expectations outputs without a human verification step
IF Great Expectations validation results are used to update travel plans or reservations
mitigations: Require human review before acting on outputs
Compare outputs against source data
Mark validation results as advisory only
Disable automatic write-back from TREK
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, email addresses, and country visit history, which can be highly sensitive. Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation and may process those files if shared. Because TREK is self-hosted and the pair lacks documented residency or retention controls, compliance breach risk is high when sensitive travel data is validated or logged.
conditions: IF EU PII or travel history is processed in TREK and then written into shared validation artifacts
IF logs or uploads retain secrets beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared validation files
Shorten log retention immediately
Redact identifiers before export
Confirm residency and retention settings
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data classification and retention
